frozen: 2026-10-20, branch fald/asf10-port, BEFORE any comparison run of the port (no gpuemu-f32 / HLSL fade code existed when this was written)
rule: These numbers are not changed after a comparison has run. A failure is investigated and reported; a tolerance is never widened.
steps: per pixel = the max over its three channels of |a - b| / spacing(|b|) in FP16 (the existing WARP replays' _steps)

off_gate.what: flank fade OFF: every field + the output frame of the 51-run matrix (tests/test_fald_fade.cpp OffMatrix) hash-equal to tests/fixtures/fald_fade_off_main.hashes (main 6273464)
off_gate.tolerance: bit for bit (every FNV-1a 64 hash equal)

gate1_f32_vs_f64.what: the float32 GPU-order port (DLC dlc/fald/fadeemu.py) against the frozen float64 study twin (r10/temu.py TEmu + r11/cands11.make_post11 + r11/T/tl11.TL11State, variant F10_TMTC), CPU, same inputs, zone drives frozen (FixedMaps: both sides' kernels see the twin's own stateless round drives)

floor_F.note: F is in nits (0.05 .. 1e4): an absolute 2e-4 on 1e4-nit values is below float32 resolution (ulp(1e4) ~ 1e-3), so the plan's 'F within 2e-4 absolute' is read as: the consumed quantity lit = smoothstep(1, 3, F) within 2e-4 absolute AND F itself within 2e-4 relative, every element

shift.used: accepted / rejected identical on every frame
shift.measure: |used shift (dy, dx) difference| per axis, 1/8-res texels, frames where both accept it
shift.note: the raw phase-correlation estimate of a REJECTED shift (e.g. a cut frame's noise peak) is a diagnostic, not compared

gate1_f32_vs_f64.study_logs: the twin run here must reproduce r11/T/out/motion11/<seq>.json F10_TMTC cutlog: cut identical, shift_used identical, used shift within 1e-6 texel (the same float64 rule; only the reduction order differs)

gate2_hlsl_vs_f32.what: the HLSL on WARP (tests/test_fald_fade.cpp dumps) against fadeemu (Emu(sampler='warp', subtexel_bits=8)), the device stateless (temporal mode off), drives recomputed by the replay as in the existing WARP replays

fade_fields.note: atol 5e-5 instead of 2e-5 as PORT_PLAN 5.2 allows for the long separable sums (sigma 32 = 257 taps); stated here before the run

floor_F_rel.note: F = exp(...) goes through a device transcendental directly (WARP's exp vs numpy's: a few ulp); 1e-5 relative is far below what lit = smoothstep(1, 3, F) can see

gate2_hlsl_vs_f32.flags: array_equal: cut, shift used, advance, has-history

cells.still_rule: a still = the first frame after a reset (no history: s = f_q, fade_T = fade)
cells.x_naninf: the sanitise cell. Gate 1 compares the fade field only (the twin's T / OF / base layer propagate NaN through torch where the HLSL's max() drops it: not a port question). Gate 2 compares the fade-stack fields everywhere and the output on pixels whose input is finite.
cells.x_odd1366: 1366 x 768 on its own 17 x 9 panel file (DLC tests/fald_fade_cells.py odd_panel.bin): gate 2 only (the study twin is 3840 x 2160 / the owner's file)

negative_control.rule: a deliberate one-constant mutation must FAIL the gate it belongs to; the code is restored and the gate passes again
mutations: gate 2 (sequence): HLSL T base rate a0 0.25 -> 0.3
